subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix be owned as a pi-tui renderer/dependency fix, an OpenClaw TUI viewport/follow-state policy, or a new explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: Source evidence shows a credible renderer and TUI state path, but the permanent fix affects terminal UX semantics and dependency ownership rather than being a narrow mechanical repair.

options.title: Fix renderer and TUI anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then keeps follow behavior only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI scroll preference
options.body: Expose explicit terminal auto-scroll control, accepting a new user-facing settings surface and fresh/upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a current-main PTY capture demonstrates the exact jump and renderer reason.

recommendation.title: Fix renderer and TUI anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then keeps follow behavior only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-source and dependency integration trail points to steipete as the best available owner for choosing whether this belongs in the renderer, OpenClaw TUI state, or product settings.
